verdict.rationale: CoreWeave documents creating CKS clusters via the Cloud Console, Terraform, or the CKS API, adding GPU Node Pools (including pay-as-you-go Spot Node Pools), and getting a kubeconfig to run workloads with kubectl. Its pricing page claims you can 'quickly spin-up burst On-Demand' GPU capacity. However, provisioning goes through a managed Kubernetes cluster and Node Pool rather than a standalone instance, and nothing evidences time-to-running-code; quota limits may also require increase requests. missing for 10: documented or hands-on evidence of minutes-level time-to-running, a simple single-instance provisioning path, explicit API-driven GPU Node Pool creation, independent corroboration.
